title: Only 7% Pass This Harvard Entrance Exam
summary: Evidence, numbers, priorities and strategic trade-offs test whether your strongest decision survives scrutiny.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge contains ten Harvard-inspired questions across analysis, evidence, quantitative reasoning, data, language and decision making. It progresses from clear individual clues to compact case-style decisions.

Choose the answer best supported by the information shown. No specialist university knowledge is required, and correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.

This is not an official Harvard University admissions test, application assessment or prediction of admission.

steps: Complete ten carefully selected questions in one focused challenge.
Choose one answer each time. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Reveal your result, skill breakdown and complete answer review after the final question.

about.disclaimer: Independent entertainment challenge. Not an official Harvard admissions test and not affiliated with any university.

harvard-s1q1.question: A team needs writing, numbers and presentation skills. Which option covers all three with the fewest people?

answers.a2: One writer and one analyst who presents

harvard-s1q2.question: A $250 budget spends 36%. How much remains?

harvard-s2q8.question: IMPARTIAL is closest in meaning to…

harvard-s2q2.question: A survey of volunteers finds 90% support. What is the biggest limitation?

answers.a3: Volunteers may not represent the whole population

harvard-s3q1.question: A project costs $18,000 and saves $3,000 per month. After how many months are costs recovered?

harvard-s3q4.question: Project A reaches 120 people for $6,000. Project B reaches 150 for $9,000. Which has lower cost per person?

harvard-s4q1.question: Two urgent tasks remain: one prevents immediate harm; the other improves next month's report. Which comes first?

harvard-s4q3.question: A proposal scores impact 7 and cost 4. Another scores impact 8 and cost 8. If higher impact and lower cost are preferred, what is true?

harvard-s5q6.question: Region A has 80 successes from 100; B has 117 from 150. Which has the higher rate, and by how much?

harvard-s5q8.question: The final rule selects the lowest-cost proposal scoring at least 15. A: cost 9, score 14. B: cost 12, score 16. C: cost 10, score 15. D: cost 8, score 13. Which is selected?
